title: It’s honestly such good vibes!! #interactive #theatre #immersive #exp...
transcript: Part interactive theater, part game, this communal experience imagines that the East River suddenly disappears one day, and it's up to us to create a new neighborhood from scratch. You select a character profile to play as, you participate in mayoral elections, and use a digital interface on your phone to vote for what to build. At which point the performers use assorted food items to construct the miniature neighborhood right before our eyes. The show is called DIRT and it's a 90 minute experience created by the company Sour Milk, where you can play along quietly with the voting if that's more your speed, or raise your voice to try to sway the group and build coalitions. I did a bit of each throughout the show and I found it incredibly fun both ways. But of course it's also a bit of a satire, pointing out the corruption, pitfalls, roadblocks, etc. that make it difficult to build a functioning community in the system we that we have. And even when we are making progress, it's messy and incomplete and impossible to please everybody. Still though, despite all of that, I found that the show left me more optimistic than anything. Cause as much as it's a highly oversimplified, lower stakes microcosm of city planning and civic engagement, the experience also reminds us that this is more or less how it works in real life. We ARE all members of a community and we DO have the capacity to use our votes and our voices to influence what we want it to look like. So for anyone who enjoys interactive theatre or live game experiences, or live game experiences, I highly recommend checking out DIRT at the Tank in New York City before it closes on February 15th.
